title: Momenergy: relativistic momentum and energy
summary: The four-momentum as the momenergy arrow; E = γmc², p = γmv and the invariant E² = p²c² + m²c⁴; the Newtonian limit; mass as invariant; massless particles; conservation of four-momentum.

objectives.description: Derive the massive energy–momentum relation and its low-speed expansion with SI units.
Transform energy and momentum together and recover a particle velocity.
Treat photon momentum as a null vector and derive Doppler/aberration relations.
Conserve total four-momentum and distinguish system invariant mass from constituent masses.

preparation.description: Read Spacetime Physics Chapter 7 Momenergy (pp. 189–220): Sections 7.1–7.7 and the exercises.
Second account: Tong, Dynamics and Relativity, Section 7.4 Relativistic Kinematics, including 7.4.4 Massless Particles (reference-only).
Optional: MIT 8.20 Week 3 videos, Lecture 9.1 Momentum Conservation and Lecture 9.2 Energy Conservation.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A fast particle has a larger invariant mass.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Its energy and momentum increase; its mass-shell invariant is unchanged.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A photon has zero energy because its mass is zero.
commonMisconceptions.correction: A nonzero null momentum has E=c|p| and positive energy.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The mass of a system is always the sum of individual rest masses.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Relative motion and internal energy contribute to the system invariant mass.
